- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (≥0.67) — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for 30d horizon if recent price > 70.00.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is falling, model overcorrects downward — increase forecast by 0.3–0.8% to avoid premature mean reversion.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after a peak, model often fails to recognize the “overshoot” — add a 1–2 day lagged correction to prevent premature decline.
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.33) and price is above 68.00, model tends to overpredict decline — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 70.00, model often underestimates volatility — increase forecast variance by 0.2–0.5% to reflect sentiment-driven risk premium.
- If true outcome shows a “rebound” after a dip, model often misses it — add a 1–2 day buffer to forecast recovery if sentiment turns positive within 3–5 days.
